newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BA to increase UK-Hong Kong cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: BA to increase UK-Hong Kong cargo flights.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo said it plans to increase its freighter service between the UK and Hong Kong to five from the present three times a week later this year

Its Greater China regional manager Chris Chan told Reuters this would be achieved by wet-leasing a second 100-tonne capacity Boeing 747-200 freighter from U.S. cargo specialist operator Atlas Air to add to the one it already uses on the route, operated via Delhi and Bahrain.
Wet-leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew and usually also includes insurance and maintenance.
From May 17, the service will move to London Stansted from London Gatwick airport.
"We hope to start in the fourth quarter, but ideally in September or even earlier than that," Chan said in an interview.
BA said it already had the necessary traffic rights under the bilateral air agreement between the UK and China to increase the frequency of its UK-HK cargo services.

Preparations are underway to apply for slots at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport, which could prove to be problematical because of the airport's notorious congestion and intense competition for slots, Chan said.
Industry observers said extra capacity on the London-Hong Kong route was bound to increase downward pressure on cargo rates.
